# google_vertex_ai_custom_job

Represents a job that runs custom workloads such as a Docker container or a
Python package. A CustomJob can have multiple worker pools and each worker
pool can have its own machine and input spec. A CustomJob will be cleaned up
once the job enters terminal state (failed or succeeded).


To get more information about CustomJob, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.customJobs)

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Custom Job Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_custom_job" "custom_job" {
  display_name = "example-custom-job"
  region       = "us-central1"

  labels = {
    env = "test"
  }

  job_spec {
    worker_pool_specs {
      replica_count = 1

      machine_spec {
        machine_type = "n1-standard-4"
      }

      disk_spec {
        boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
        boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      }

      container_spec {
        image_uri = "us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/training/tf-cpu.2-8.py310:latest"
        command   = ["echo", "test"]
        args      = ["--epochs=1"]

        env {
          name  = "TEST_ENV"
          value = "test_val"
        }
      }
    }

    scheduling {
      timeout                       = "86400s"
      restart_job_on_worker_restart = false
      strategy                      = "STANDARD"
    }

    base_output_directory {
      output_uri_prefix = "gs://${google_storage_bucket.job_bucket.name}/custom-job-output"
    }
  }
}

resource "google_storage_bucket" "job_bucket" {
  name     = "example-custom-job-bucket"
  location = "US-CENTRAL1"
  force_destroy = true
  uniform_bucket_level_access = true
}
```

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Custom Job Python Package


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_custom_job" "custom_job" {
  display_name = "example-custom-job-python"
  region       = "us-central1"

  encryption_spec {
    kms_key_name = "example-key"
  }

  job_spec {
    service_account         = google_service_account.custom_job_sa.email
    tensorboard             = google_vertex_ai_tensorboard.tensorboard.id
    enable_web_access       = true
    enable_dashboard_access = true

    base_output_directory {
      output_uri_prefix = "gs://${google_storage_bucket.job_bucket.name}/custom-job-output"
    }

    psc_interface_config {
      network_attachment = "projects/${data.google_project.project.project_id}/regions/us-central1/networkAttachments/example-attachment"

      dns_peering_configs {
        domain         = "example.com."
        target_project = data.google_project.project.project_id
        target_network = "default"
      }
    }

    scheduling {
      timeout                       = "86400s"
      restart_job_on_worker_restart = false
      strategy                      = "FLEX_START"
      disable_retries               = true
      max_wait_duration             = "1800s"
    }

    worker_pool_specs {
      replica_count = 1

      machine_spec {
        machine_type      = "g2-standard-4"
        accelerator_type  = "NVIDIA_L4"
        accelerator_count = 1
      }

      disk_spec {
        boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
        boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      }

      python_package_spec {
        executor_image_uri = "us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/training/tf-gpu.2-12.py310:latest"
        package_uris       = ["gs://${google_storage_bucket.job_bucket.name}/${google_storage_bucket_object.trainer_package.name}"]
        python_module      = "trainer.task"
        args               = ["--epochs=1"]

        env {
          name  = "PYTHON_ENV"
          value = "test_val"
        }
      }

      nfs_mounts {
        server      = "10.0.0.1"
        path        = "/nfs_share"
        mount_point = "nfs_mount"
      }

      lustre_mounts {
        instance_ip   = "10.0.0.1"
        volume_handle = "lustre-vol"
        filesystem    = "lustrefs"
        mount_point   = "lustre_mount"
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.crypto_key,
  ]
}

resource "google_service_account" "custom_job_sa" {
  account_id   = "job-sa"
  display_name = "Custom Job Service Account"
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_tensorboard" "tensorboard" {
  display_name = "example-tensorboard"
  region       = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_storage_bucket" "job_bucket" {
  name                        = "example-custom-job-python-bucket"
  location                    = "US-CENTRAL1"
  force_destroy               = true
  uniform_bucket_level_access = true
}

resource "google_storage_bucket_object" "trainer_package" {
  name    = "trainer-0.1.tar.gz"
  bucket  = google_storage_bucket.job_bucket.name
  content = "placeholder"
}

resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "crypto_key" {
  crypto_key_id = "example-key"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member        = "serviceAccount:service-${data.google_project.project.number}@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}

data "google_project" "project" {}
```

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Custom Job Tpu Network


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_custom_job" "custom_job" {
  display_name = "example-custom-job-tpu"
  region       = "us-central1"

  job_spec {
    network            = "projects/${data.google_project.project.number}/global/networks/${google_compute_network.vertex_network.name}"
    reserved_ip_ranges = [google_compute_global_address.vertex_range.name]

    worker_pool_specs {
      replica_count = 1

      machine_spec {
        machine_type = "n1-standard-4"
        tpu_topology = "2x2"

        reservation_affinity {
          reservation_affinity_type = "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"
          key                       = "compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name"
          values                    = ["projects/${data.google_project.project.number}/zones/us-central1-z/reservations/example-reservation"]
        }
      }

      disk_spec {
        boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
        boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      }

      container_spec {
        image_uri = "us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/training/tf-cpu.2-12.py310:latest"
        command   = ["echo", "test"]
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_service_networking_connection.vertex_vpc_connection,
  ]
}

resource "google_compute_network" "vertex_network" {
  name                    = "custom-job-vpc-net"
  auto_create_subnetworks = false
}

resource "google_compute_global_address" "vertex_range" {
  name          = "custom-job-vpc-range"
  purpose       = "VPC_PEERING"
  address_type  = "INTERNAL"
  prefix_length = 24
  network       = google_compute_network.vertex_network.id
}

resource "google_service_networking_connection" "vertex_vpc_connection" {
  network                 = google_compute_network.vertex_network.id
  service                 = "servicenetworking.googleapis.com"
  reserved_peering_ranges = [google_compute_global_address.vertex_range.name]
}

data "google_project" "project" {}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the CustomJob.
  The name can be up to 128 characters long and can consist of any UTF-8 characters.

* `job_spec` -
  (Required)
  Job spec.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec).

* `region` -
  (Required)
  The Google Cloud region to run the custom job in.


* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The labels with user-defined metadata to organize CustomJobs.
  Label keys and values can be no longer than 64 characters (Unicode codepoints), can only contain lowercase letters, numeric characters, underscores and dashes. International characters are allowed.
  See https://goo.gl/xmQnxf for more information and examples of labels.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `encryption_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Customer-managed encryption key options for a CustomJob.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_encryption_spec).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_job_spec"></a>The `job_spec` block supports:

* `worker_pool_specs` -
  (Required)
  The spec of the worker pools including machine type and Docker image.
  All worker pools except the first one are optional and can be skipped by providing an empty value.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs).

* `scheduling` -
  (Optional)
  Scheduling options for a CustomJob.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_scheduling).

* `service_account` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the service account for workload run-as account.

* `network` -
  (Optional)
  The full name of the Compute Engine network to which the Job should be peered.

* `reserved_ip_ranges` -
  (Optional)
  A list of names for the reserved ip ranges under the VPC network that can be used for this job.

* `psc_interface_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for PSC-I for CustomJob.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_psc_interface_config).

* `base_output_directory` -
  (Optional)
  The Cloud Storage location to store the output of this CustomJob or HyperparameterTuningJob.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_base_output_directory).

* `tensorboard` -
  (Optional)
  The name of a Vertex AI Tensorboard resource to which this CustomJob will upload Tensorboard logs.

* `enable_web_access` -
  (Optional)
  Whether you want Vertex AI to enable interactive shell access to training containers.

* `enable_dashboard_access` -
  (Optional)
  Whether you want Vertex AI to enable access to the customized dashboard in training chief container.


<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs"></a>The `worker_pool_specs` block supports:

* `replica_count` -
  (Optional)
  The number of worker replicas to use for this worker pool.

* `machine_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Specification of a single machine.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_machine_spec).

* `disk_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Disk spec.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_disk_spec).

* `container_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The custom container task. Either `container_spec` or `python_package_spec` can be provided, but not both.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_container_spec).

* `python_package_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The Python packaged task. Either `container_spec` or `python_package_spec` can be provided, but not both.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_python_package_spec).

* `nfs_mounts` -
  (Optional)
  List of NFS mount spec.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_nfs_mounts).

* `lustre_mounts` -
  (Optional)
  List of Lustre mounts.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_lustre_mounts).


<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_machine_spec"></a>The `machine_spec` block supports:

* `machine_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type of the machine.

* `accelerator_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type of accelerator(s) that may be attached to the machine.

* `accelerator_count` -
  (Optional)
  The number of accelerators to attach to the machine.

* `tpu_topology` -
  (Optional)
  The topology of the TPUs.

* `reservation_affinity` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for using robust to failure reservation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_machine_spec_reservation_affinity).


<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_machine_spec_reservation_affinity"></a>The `reservation_affinity` block supports:

* `reservation_affinity_type` -
  (Required)
  Specifies the reservation affinity type. Possible values: "NO_RESERVATION", "ANY_RESERVATION", and "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"

* `key` -
  (Optional)
  Corresponds to the label key of a reservation resource.

* `values` -
  (Optional)
  Corresponds to the label values of a reservation resource.

<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_disk_spec"></a>The `disk_spec` block supports:

* `boot_disk_type` -
  (Optional)
  Type of the disk. The default value depends on the machine type. Valid values include: "pd-ssd", "pd-standard", "pd-balanced", and "hyperdisk-balanced".

* `boot_disk_size_gb` -
  (Optional)
  Size in GB of the boot disk (default is 100GB).

<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_container_spec"></a>The `container_spec` block supports:

* `image_uri` -
  (Required)
  The URI of a container image in the Container Registry that is to be run on each worker replica.

* `command` -
  (Optional)
  The command to be invoked when the container is started. It overrides the entrypoint instruction in Dockerfile when provided.

* `args` -
  (Optional)
  The arguments to be passed when starting the container.

* `env` -
  (Optional)
  Environment variables to be passed to the container. Maximum limit is 100.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_container_spec_env).


<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_container_spec_env"></a>The `env` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier.

* `value` -
  (Required)
  Variables that reference a $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the previous defined environment variables in the container.

<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_python_package_spec"></a>The `python_package_spec` block supports:

* `executor_image_uri` -
  (Required)
  The URI of a container image in Artifact Registry that will run the provided Python package.

* `package_uris` -
  (Required)
  The Google Cloud Storage location of the Python package files which are the training program and its dependent packages.

* `python_module` -
  (Required)
  The Python module name to run after installing the packages.

* `args` -
  (Optional)
  Command line arguments to be passed to the Python task.

* `env` -
  (Optional)
  Environment variables to be passed to the python module. Maximum limit is 100.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_python_package_spec_env).


<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_python_package_spec_env"></a>The `env` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  Name of the environment variable.

* `value` -
  (Required)
  Value of the environment variable.

<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_nfs_mounts"></a>The `nfs_mounts` block supports:

* `server` -
  (Required)
  IP address of the NFS server.

* `path` -
  (Required)
  Source path exported from NFS database.

* `mount_point` -
  (Required)
  Destination mount path. The path must be absolute.

<a name="nested_job_spec_worker_pool_specs_lustre_mounts"></a>The `lustre_mounts` block supports:

* `instance_ip` -
  (Required)
  IP address of the Lustre instance.

* `volume_handle` -
  (Required)
  The unique identifier of the Lustre volume.

* `filesystem` -
  (Required)
  The name of the Lustre filesystem.

* `mount_point` -
  (Required)
  Destination mount path. The Lustre file system will be mounted for the user under /mnt/lustre/<mount_point>.

<a name="nested_job_spec_scheduling"></a>The `scheduling` block supports:

* `timeout` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum job running time. The default is 7 days. A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".

* `restart_job_on_worker_restart` -
  (Optional)
  Restarts the entire CustomJob if a worker gets restarted.

* `strategy` -
  (Optional)
  This determines which type of scheduling strategy to use. Possible values: ["STANDARD", "SPOT", "FLEX_START"]

* `disable_retries` -
  (Optional)
  Indicates if the job should retry for internal errors after the job starts running.

* `max_wait_duration` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum duration that a job will wait for the requested resources to be provisioned if the scheduling strategy is set to FLEX_START.

<a name="nested_job_spec_psc_interface_config"></a>The `psc_interface_config` block supports:

* `network_attachment` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the attachment to connect to.

* `dns_peering_configs` -
  (Optional)
  DNS peering config for the PSC interface.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_job_spec_psc_interface_config_dns_peering_configs).


<a name="nested_job_spec_psc_interface_config_dns_peering_configs"></a>The `dns_peering_configs` block supports:

* `domain` -
  (Required)
  The DNS name suffix of the zone being peered to, e.g., "my-internal-domain.corp.". Must end with a dot.

* `target_project` -
  (Required)
  The project ID hosting the Cloud DNS managed zone that contains the 'domain'. The Vertex AI Service Agent requires the dns.peer role on this project.

* `target_network` -
  (Required)
  The VPC network name in the target_project where the DNS zone specified by 'domain' is visible.

<a name="nested_job_spec_base_output_directory"></a>The `base_output_directory` block supports:

* `output_uri_prefix` -
  (Required)
  Cloud Storage folder URL to store the output.

<a name="nested_encryption_spec"></a>The `encryption_spec` block supports:

* `kms_key_name` -
  (Required)
  Resource name of the Cloud KMS key used to protect the resource.
  The Cloud KMS key must be in the same region as the resource. It must have the format
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{key_ring}/cryptoKeys/{crypto_key}`.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/customJobs/{{name}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the CustomJob.

* `state` -
  The detailed state of the job.

* `create_time` -
  Time when the CustomJob was created.

* `start_time` -
  Time when the CustomJob for the first time entered the `JOB_STATE_RUNNING` state.

* `end_time` -
  Time when the CustomJob entered any of the following states: `JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED`, `JOB_STATE_FAILED`, `JOB_STATE_CANCELLED`.

* `update_time` -
  Time when the CustomJob was most recently updated.

* `error` -
  Only populated when job's state is `JOB_STATE_FAILED` or `JOB_STATE_CANCELLED`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_error).

* `web_access_uris` -
  URIs for accessing interactive shells (one URI for each training node).

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


<a name="nested_error"></a>The `error` block contains:

* `code` -
  (Output)
  The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.

* `message` -
  (Output)
  A developer-facing error message, which should be in English.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 0 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


CustomJob can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/customJobs/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import CustomJob using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-optional value->"
    region = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import CustomJob using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/customJobs/{{name}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), CustomJob can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/customJobs/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default {{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_custom_job.default {{name}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
